hints: Focus on what the pH tells you about the type of oxide Y must be, acidic or basic.
Recall how Period 3 oxides change from basic on the left to acidic on the right, and which ones actually react with water.
Use the clue that Y is a solid to rule out the non-metal whose oxide is a gas at room temperature, leaving the solid acidic oxide.
walkthrough:
**Translate the pH clue**

Think like this, pH less than 7 means acidic. So Y must be an acidic oxide that reacts with water to make an acid.

General rule:
$$\text{acidic oxide} + \text{H}_2\text{O} \rightarrow \text{acid solution (pH < 7)}$$

**Recall Period 3 oxide trend**

Across Period 3, oxides go from basic to amphoteric to acidic. Left side metals make basic oxides, right side non-metals make acidic oxides.

For example:
$$\text{Na}_2\text{O} + \text{H}_2\text{O} \rightarrow 2\text{NaOH (pH > 7)}$$

**Apply the solid Y clue**

Both phosphorus and sulfur make acidic oxides, but sulfur burning mainly gives $\text{SO}_2$, which is a gas, not a solid. Silicon makes $\text{SiO}_2$, a solid, but it is insoluble and does not react with water.

Phosphorus fits perfectly:
$$\text{P}_4 + 5\text{O}_2 \rightarrow \text{P}_4\text{O}_{10} \text{(solid)}$$

**Check the reaction with water**

Solid phosphorus(V) oxide reacts vigorously with water to give phosphoric acid, a solution with pH well below 7.
$$\text{P}_4\text{O}_{10} + 6\text{H}_2\text{O} \rightarrow 4\text{H}_3\text{PO}_4$$

options.A: Incorrect. Sodium forms $\text{Na}_2\text{O}$, a solid basic oxide. With water it gives $\text{NaOH}$, a strong alkali with pH much greater than 7, the opposite of what is observed.
options.B: Incorrect. Silicon forms $\text{SiO}_2$, a solid acidic oxide, but it is a giant covalent solid that is insoluble and does not react with water. It cannot produce an acidic solution.
options.C: Correct. Phosphorus forms solid $\text{P}_4\text{O}_{10}$. This reacts with water to form phosphoric acid, $\text{H}_3\text{PO}_4$, giving a solution with pH less than 7. It satisfies both the solid Y and acidic solution clues.
options.D: Incorrect. Sulfur does form acidic oxides that give pH less than 7, but its main combustion product $\text{SO}_2$ is a gas, not a solid. This fails the first clue that Y is a solid.
